items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: we were playing stage band instrumental, the instrumental music of popular tunes, like “Beat It” or “Billy Jean” by Michael Jackson.

ctx.x: Yeah. I have to chuckle because you know most of the fellas I’ve talked to are considerably older. For you to say the popular music of the day is Kiss — it’s something different you know. That’s very interesting though. Your friends at the time probably did not share your growing enthusiasm for jazz music?

Well they did, we had what was called a jazz band, our stage band. But the thing was we weren’t playing the music of Duke Ellington, Count Basie or Benny Goodman, Fletcher Henderson, we were playing stage band instrumental, the instrumental music of popular tunes, like “Beat It” or “Billy Jean” by Michael Jackson. Every now and then a piece of Duke Ellington’s music would wind up in their book but we didn’t really, we weren’t really into it. So I mean we called it jazz because it was instrumental music without…

that I got from the crowd was a lot of the high school students coming to see the students from their feeder school that were going to come, they said we’re getting two classes of musicians, let’s see what’s going to be coming to the high school. They enjoyed it, they clapped and I said oh, this is a great feeling. I said I think I want to be a jazz musician one day. And you know I went through a thing where I wanted to be a boxer, I wanted to be a truck driver, I wanted to play football, but of all of those…
